title: Trust by Design LinkedIn Post
body:
Something we see often in Muslim matrimony: trust is assumed until it is broken.

We built Date Khaas on a different assumption — that trust must be *earned*, feature by feature, before a single introduction is made.

Here is what that looks like in practice:

🔒 **Photos blurred by default** — a profile image is unlocked only when both sides show genuine intent. No browsing. No screenshot culture. Your face is an amanah.

✅ **Identity verification beyond OTP** — real documents are checked so that the name on the profile belongs to the face in the photo.

👨‍👩‍👧 **Wali involvement built in** — a parent or guardian gets read-only visibility of matches. Because in Islam, nikah is never just between two people.

💬 **Conversations stay on platform** — so if something feels wrong, there is a full record to act on.

The matrimony space has trained people to treat catfishing as a cost of doing business. We disagree. Safety is not a premium feature. It is the foundation everything else rests on.

If you are building in the Muslim lifestyle, halal-tech, or trust-and-safety space and thinking about how to design for dignity, I would love to hear how you approach it.

#MuslimMatrimony #Nikah #TrustAndSafety #IslamicMarriage #HalalTech

research_sources.insight: NRI Muslim diaspora in the Gulf and UK/US is peak-intent in summer 2026 — professionals visiting home seek trusted introductions. Marketing to 'NRI moment' converts.
Photo blur is the #1 emerging trust differentiator for Muslim matrimony 2026: Muzz, Salams, AlKhattaba, Oolfa all now offer default or opt-in photo blurring as a modesty and safety feature.
Wali (guardian) invite features are now expected by serious users — Salams Premium gives wali read-only chat access; Pure Matrimony and SalafiMatch have built-in wali involvement flows.

Competitor claim to answer: NikahForever claims '100% privacy guaranteed and verified profiles' but verification appears OTP-level. Shaadi.com leans on 'millions of success stories' rather than safety-first messaging.

Catfishing and romance scams in Muslim matrimony are well-documented — platforms that keep conversations on-platform, mandate video verification, and use AI detection retain more users past the first match.
